So AuthCookie is only set in one place in Globals.cs and bound through the ConfigurableBinder. There's no other code path that could re-randomize it, which means the flip I saw earlier must have a different explanation. Let me look back at the initial request sequence — the first curl to /app with the cookie showed the full admin layout with the navbar, "Admin" auth row, and the "nothing at this address" message, which was the /app NotFound page rendered in Admin mode. Then /app/ with the cookie showed the non-admin branch instead, which is strange since it's the same endpoint with the same cookie. The /app route without a trailing slash doesn't match the "/" route, so it hits NotFound and renders the admin shell. But then the cookie stopped working entirely — even /app with the cookie showed NOADMIN afterward, and 10 out of 10 requests failed. This flip is puzzling since nothing on disk changed and the log shows no restart, so either the first admin render was a fluke or something else is going on with how the cookie is being validated.

I'm wondering if there's a startup race condition: the binder loads config and sets AuthCookie, but maybe the first request arrived before the static initialization finished, or there's something about how the configuration gets loaded. Actually, wait — I think I'm seeing a pattern here. The first request with the cookie hit /app and rendered the admin shell, but then the second request to /app/ immediately after showed no admin. That's a flip right at the very start of my testing. So the admin cookie matched exactly once, then stopped matching — and after that, it never matched again, even on the first /app/ request I made.

Maybe the running server's AuthCookie isn't actually what I think it is. I've been assuming it's bound to that specific value from appsettings.json, but if it's something else entirely, the first request shouldn't have worked either. Unless the first request worked because of a different mechanism. Let me test whether a random 20-character cookie also renders admin — that would tell me whether any cookie matches or if it's specifically that value. I should also check if there's something about how Blazor prerendering and HttpContext work that could explain this behavior.

Actually, I think I'm seeing a pattern here. The first admin render happened on the first request to /app, and every subsequent request to any path shows NOADMIN. That's suspicious. Maybe there's a startup race condition: the Globals.AuthCookie field initializer generates a random value at assembly load, then the binder tries to set it from config, but if a request arrives and triggers access to the Globals type before the binder finishes, the field might still be random. But that doesn't quite fit because the log shows "Serving public files from /app" after the database setup, which means the binder had already run and set AuthCookie to the appsettings value. And the app was already listening when I sent my first request — I had slept 20 seconds after startup, so the app was fully initialized. So the first request should have worked if AuthCookie was properly set, and it did.

Wait, but the /app/ request right after showed NOADMIN with the same cookie. Same process, same cookie, seconds apart. That shouldn't happen. Unless the first admin response wasn't actually from the main server process — maybe there's a race condition where two processes are competing for port 5195, or maybe the cookie isn't being sent with the second request even though I'm passing it the same way. I should test this right now with the running server: send multiple requests to /app with that exact cookie, plus try some random cookies, and check the server log for any errors or warnings after each one.

I'm also wondering if this is a Blazor prerendering issue where the HttpContext gets consumed or reused somehow, or if there's an `AddScoped<IHttpContextAccessor>` that's not configured correctly. Let me also run a quick test with curl using a cookie jar to rule out any curl-specific behavior. And I need to think about whether there's a second `Globals` type in scope — `Bovis.Web.Globals` is internal to Bovis.Web.dll, but UserContext references it by full name, so that should be fine. The binder might be binding to the right property, but maybe there's a path construction issue with how the assembly attribute name is being resolved.

Actually, I think I've found something: the binder is configured to only set values if they exist in the config (`if (cval == null) continue;`), so it never overwrites what's already there. That means if AuthCookie was already set to a random value, the binder shouldn't touch it. But the log showed PublicBaseUrl as "/app", which is the appsettings value, not the default — so the binder definitely did run and set something. The key insight is that "Serving public files from /app" happens before `app.Run()`, after all the builder setup, so the binder had already finished by then. So AuthCookie should have been set to the appsettings value before the app started listening.

Let me test whether the first render that matched the cookie was actually correct or if something else is going on. I'll try hitting the endpoint with different cookie values — the appsettings one, a random 20-char one, and the random 10-char one from the list-configs output — and see if they all return NOADMIN or if something unexpected happens. That'll tell me whether the server's AuthCookie is actually the appsettings value or if it's stuck on some random value instead. I'm realizing the cookie might not have been sent at all due to a shell variable issue, but that doesn't explain the admin render. Let me think through the actual flow: the server binds AuthCookie from appsettings before starting to listen, so requests should work. But if the first request succeeded and later ones failed, something must have changed in between—either the binding didn't happen at all, or the static Globals type got re-initialized somehow, which shouldn't be possible without a process restart.

Actually, I think I've found it. The binder might be operating on a different Globals class entirely. If the codebase has multiple [Configurable] classes—like Bovis.Storage.Globals—and one of them has a field that maps to the "Bovis.Web:AuthCookie" key, the binder could be writing the appsettings value into the wrong object. That would explain why the running server never actually got the appsettings value; it's stuck with the random default from initialization, which is why my cookie attempts all failed.

But wait—the log clearly shows PublicBaseUrl is set to "/app", so the running Globals.Web definitely got the appsettings value. If the binder set PublicBaseUrl correctly, it should have set AuthCookie too since they're both [Configurable] fields in the same class. The only way this makes sense is if PublicBaseUrl was being read from a different source than AuthCookie. I need to check whether there's another code path that reads PublicBaseUrl directly from configuration—like a Controller or the _Host template using the configuration store directly instead of the static Globals.Web.PublicBaseUrl field.

Now I'm puzzled why subsequent requests show NOADMIN with the same cookie — the server's AuthCookie value must have changed between the first and second request, or there's a race condition where the binder hadn't finished setting the value from config yet when the first request came in.

That doesn't match. I need to check if there's another binder invocation happening somewhere — maybe in `CreateAndSetupBuilder` or a second builder setup — that could be overwriting the AuthCookie with a different value. The `list-configs` command doesn't create a binder at all, which explains why it showed a random value, but the server command might be creating multiple builders or re-binding the configuration. I'm checking the binder's logic to see if it's properly setting the AuthCookie value from configuration. The binder iterates through all loaded assemblies and applies configuration values to matching fields, but I need to verify whether it's actually populating the AuthCookie or if there's a mismatch in how the property is being resolved.
